facts.fact_text: The applicant took part in the public demonstration at Basse-Terre on 12 February 1983.
The applicant carried a placard during the public demonstration at Basse-Terre on 12 February 1983.
The demonstration on 12 February 1983 took the form of a procession through the streets of Basse-Terre.

The Principal Public Prosecutor's complaint of 1 June 1983 alleged a breach under Article 106 of Decree no. 72-468 of 9 June 1972 and requested that disciplinary proceedings be brought against Mr Ezelin before the Bar Council.
The Basse-Terre Court of Appeal's judgment of 12 December 1983 sentenced Mr Ezelin to the disciplinary penalty of a reprimand and awarded costs against him.
The Principal Public Prosecutor's complaint of 1 June 1983 was brought under Article 113 of Decree no. 72-468 of 9 June 1972 regulating the profession of avocat.

Article 106 of Decree no. 72-468 of 9 June 1972 regulating the profession of avocat provides that any contravention of statutes or regulations, infringement of professional rules or breach of integrity, honour or discretion, even relating to non-professional matters, shall render the avocat responsible liable to the disciplinary sanctions listed in Article 107.

The Principal Public Prosecutor's complaint of 1 June 1983 alleged a breach under Article 106 of Decree no. 72-468 of 9 June 1972 and requested that disciplinary proceedings be brought against Mr Ezelin before the Bar Council.

The Bar Council's decision of 25 July 1983 found that it did not appear from the judicial investigation that Mr Ezelin committed a breach of Article 106 of Decree no. 72-468 of 9 June 1972 in connection with taking part in the demonstration, and that no disciplinary sanction could consequently be imposed on him for that conduct.
The Bar Council's decision of 25 July 1983 noted that the judicial investigation had been brought to an end with a discharge order that had become final.

In its report of 14 December 1989 made under Article 31 of the Convention, the European Commission of Human Rights expressed the opinion that there had been a breach of Article 11 of the Convention, by fifteen votes to six.
